title: Chlorite maximum contaminant level: 1.0 mg/L for systems using chlorine dioxide, three-sample set average

conditions: Community and nontransient noncommunity water systems using chlorine dioxide for disinfection or oxidation (141.132(b)(2))
exclusions: Systems that do not use chlorine dioxide are not required to monitor for chlorite; transient noncommunity systems using chlorine dioxide are reached by subpart L for the chlorine dioxide MRDL in 141.65 (141.130(a)(2)), while chlorite monitoring applies to community and nontransient noncommunity systems (141.132(b)(2))

claims.subject: Routine daily chlorite monitoring
claims.value: Daily samples at the entrance to the distribution system; any daily sample exceeding the chlorite MCL requires additional distribution system samples the following day

conditions: Community and nontransient noncommunity water systems using chlorine dioxide for disinfection or oxidation (141.132(b)(2))
exclusions: Systems that do not use chlorine dioxide are not required to monitor for chlorite; transient noncommunity systems using chlorine dioxide are reached by subpart L for the chlorine dioxide MRDL in 141.65 (141.130(a)(2)), while chlorite monitoring applies to community and nontransient noncommunity systems (141.132(b)(2))

claims.subject: Routine monthly chlorite monitoring
claims.value: A three-sample set each month in the distribution system: one sample near the first customer, one at a location representative of average residence time, one at a location reflecting maximum residence time; any additional routine sampling is conducted in the same manner, as three-sample sets at those locations
conditions: The term three-sample set is also recorded on page dbp.definitions (claim.dbp.definitions.chlorite-three-sample-set)

claims.subject: Additional chlorite monitoring after an entrance exceedance
claims.value: On each day following a routine entrance sample that exceeds the chlorite MCL, three distribution system samples: as close to the first customer as possible, at average residence time, and as close to the end of the distribution system as possible

conditions: Community and nontransient noncommunity water systems using chlorine dioxide for disinfection or oxidation (141.132(b)(2))

claims.subject: Reduced chlorite monitoring
claims.value: Entrance monitoring may not be reduced; distribution system monitoring may be reduced to one three-sample set per quarter after one year of monitoring in which no individual routine distribution system sample taken under 141.132(b)(2)(i)(B) exceeded the chlorite MCL and the system was not required to conduct additional monitoring under 141.132(b)(2)(ii)
conditions: The system must revert to routine monitoring if any of the three quarterly distribution system samples exceeds the MCL or additional monitoring is triggered (141.132(b)(2)(iii)(B), second sentence)

claims.subject: Chlorite MCL violation
claims.value: The arithmetic average of any three-sample set exceeds the MCL; the system must notify the public under subpart Q and report to the State under 141.134
conditions: A single daily entrance sample above the MCL triggers additional monitoring the following day (141.132(b)(2)(i)(A)); it is not by itself an MCL violation
